links.comparator_used: Six expert human clinicians rating the same responses across 11 criteria (Med-PaLM 2-adapted framework)
links.outcome: Agreement of LLM-judge scores with human expert evaluations across 11 criteria
links.effect: Best LLM-judge (Claude-4.1-Opus) achieved human-equivalent evaluations on only 4 of 11 criteria; GPT-5 was consistently overcritical and Gemini-2.5-Pro overly lenient
links.tradeoff: Performance and cost-effectiveness deteriorated substantially when moving from English to Kinyarwanda inputs; sensitivity to linguistic and cultural context
links.quote: Our results show that even the highest-performing LLM-judge (Claude-4.1-Opus) achieved human-equivalent evaluations on only four of eleven criteria.

links.outcome: Agreement of LLM-judge evaluations after combining several LLMs into “LLM juries”
links.effect: LLM juries improved agreement on only one additional criterion.
links.quote: Constructing “LLM juries” to balance model-specific biases improved agreement on only one additional criterion.

design_hint: LLM-as-a-judge evaluation versus human clinician review of outputs
